official_source_checks.source: Nasdaq Trader Trading Halt Search/RSS documentation
official_source_checks.finding: official historical halt records are available and include halt/resumption fields; this is the auxiliary authority for halt-vs-missing classification

M2.conclusion: Five January securities absent from current active universe were identified, but the 7G-R artifact did not contain five issuer-level official delisting records. Do not upgrade this to PASS by inference.

M3.conclusion: 7G-R did not produce the required three listing-boundary samples. Provider reference capability is adequate but this specific sample test remains incomplete.

M4.conclusion: Three stable CIK/FIGI identity changes were observed across dated universes; exact event-date evidence remains a separate SEC/reference concern.

M5.conclusion: Five reverse-split records were sampled. BVC and CANF directly demonstrated raw pre-split prices with adjusted=false versus split-adjusted historical prices with adjusted=true. Three 2026-01-02 cases used 2026-01-01 as the prior business day, which was a market holiday, so the original runner cannot support a five-of-five empirical PASS. Massive official documentation independently confirms adjusted=false semantics.

M6.conclusion: BVC and CANF empirically show raw integer pre-split volume under adjusted=false while adjusted=true rescales volume (BVC 17,566,372 raw vs 1,756,637.2 adjusted; CANF 2,776,818 raw vs 138,840.9 adjusted). Massive flat-file documentation explicitly states prices and volumes are unadjusted. Five-of-five independent tape cross-check was not completed, so status remains PARTIAL.

M8.conclusion: Historical records consistently expose primary_exchange and type, including XNAS/XNYS/XASE and CS/ETF/ADRC/WARRANT/PFD/UNIT. These fields are suitable as provider classification inputs, but exclusion logic must retain an UNKNOWN/AMBIGUOUS path and should not treat provider type as an SEC fact.

M9.conclusion: Architecture validation PASS, not a Massive-only data PASS: Nasdaq Trader is frozen as the authoritative auxiliary source for halt-vs-missing classification. Massive OHLCV absence alone must never be classified as a halt. Historical halt search/RSS supports halt date, reason and resumption fields.

M10.conclusion: Core Basic functionality required from the market-data provider is operational: dated universe pagination and adjusted=false OHLCV. At approximately 13 universe pages per trading day, 21 January sessions imply about 273 universe calls or 54.6 minutes at 5 calls/min. This is slow but viable for month-by-month offline reconstruction; a paid tier is an optimization, not a current data entitlement requirement.

SEC: issuer identity and official corporate-event evidence

limitations: Massive historical reference is treated as VENDOR_RECONSTRUCTED_PIT, not native publication-time PIT.
M2 and M3 sample-level official cross-checks remain incomplete and must be audited during January ingestion QA rather than silently promoted to PASS.
M5/M6 runner had a holiday-calendar defect for 2026-01-02 reverse splits; this does not invalidate Massive adjusted=false semantics but prevents a five-of-five empirical PASS from that artifact.
A missing Massive daily bar is not sufficient evidence of a trading halt.
Provider security type is a classification input; UNKNOWN/AMBIGUOUS must remain explicit.
